summary: container_published_on and published_ports in up.sh and down.sh read HostConfig.PortBindings for 4222/tcp through one docker container inspect --format Go template (one host port per binding, per line) instead of the runtime port map, which Docker empties when a container stops. The comparison rule is unchanged (at least one line, every line numeric and equal to the configured port; failed inspect / no binding / non-numeric = refusal). ensure_nats's order is unchanged (existence, ownership, .State.Running, start or REUSED) and its refusal now reads `NATS container <name> is published on port <ports>, not the configured NATS port <port>`. down.sh's legacy fallback needed only the read change (rm -f already removes a stopped container).

realDockerProof.box: Docker version 29.7.2, build a7dcaa6; scratch container legion-87-impl-probe, `-p 14987:4222 nats:2.10 -js`, removed afterwards (docker ps -a shows none). The two live rigs' containers (legion-smoke-nats-sjawhar820 on 14322, legion-smoke-nats-sjawhar1083 on 14283) were not touched.
realDockerProof.running:
$ docker container inspect --format "$template" legion-87-impl-probe   # running
14987$
$
$ docker container inspect --format {{.State.Running}} legion-87-impl-probe
true
realDockerProof.stopped:
$ docker container inspect --format "$template" legion-87-impl-probe   # stopped
14987$
$
$ docker container inspect --format {{.State.Running}} legion-87-impl-probe
false
$ docker container inspect --format {{json .HostConfig.PortBindings}} legion-87-impl-probe
{"4222/tcp":[{"HostIp":"","HostPort":"14987"}]}
$ docker container inspect --format {{json .NetworkSettings.Ports}} legion-87-impl-probe   # the runtime port map, empty once stopped
{}
realDockerProof.note: Output shown through `cat -A`: `14987$` is the port plus the template's own newline, the following `$` is the one trailing newline `--format` appends; `$(...)` strips it so no empty line reaches the loop. Identical bytes running and stopped.
realDockerProof.functionDrive: Against the STOPPED probe, sourcing only the two functions from down.sh (byte-identical to up.sh's): `container_published_on legion-87-impl-probe 14987` → owned; `… 1` → refused; `… 1498` (prefix) → refused; `… 4987` (suffix) → refused; `published_ports legion-87-impl-probe` → 14987. Errors row 2 (created without -p): container_published_on refused, published_ports → none. Errors row 1 (container removed): refused, none.

trickyParts: The harness fakes match the whole `$*` argv against a single-quoted case pattern the unquoted heredoc expands from `ports_template`; the generated fake holds literal `$port`/`$bindings`/`\n` inside single quotes, so any byte difference between a script's template and the harness's fails the reuse case (deliberate drift detection).

jj here has split.legacy-bookmark-behavior: after each `jj split` the bookmark followed the remainder, so every commit was `split -m … <paths>` then `bookmark set legion/LEGION-87 -r @- --allow-backwards`.

`main@origin` advanced past this branch's base while implementing (now at 178909e0); no rebase — GitHub decides CONFLICTING, and a plain `--from main@origin` diff shows main's newer files as deletions, which is why the fork_point form is the right scope check.
deviations: README line 150 (the `SMOKE_DIR`/ports paragraph) quoted the old refusal `is not mapped to configured port <NATS_PORT>`; the plan's README task named only lines 152 and 166.
